entries.topic: Synthesis: the five front-hypothesis tests scored against Parts 2–18; the verdict and its strength

claims.text: On the five tests fixed in Part One, no test favours the front reading: the private record published (Herzl diary 1904; ADSS letters of 1943; Irish files 1948–49) matches the public refusal or is harder; 1917 warmth is one party's report and the 1944 note is unverified.

No transfer of money or favours from the Holy See to the Zionist movement or Israel is documented; the 1949 Pontifical Mission for Palestine aided Palestinian refugees; Rothschild loans ran from banks to the Papal States 1831–1850s and the borrower ended in 1870; the 2026 IOR chair's former employer is a career fact.

Shifts in the Holy See's position followed its stated interests and the Palestinian track (1967 Jerusalem statute; 1984 naming of Israel with a Palestinian homeland; talks after Madrid 1991; recognition after the Israel–PLO letters of September 1993); Israeli public pressure in 1982 and 1987 did not move it.

The Fundamental Agreement secured Church institutions (Arts 3, 4, 10) and in Art. 11 kept the Holy See 'a stranger to all merely temporal conflicts' over 'disputed territories and unsettled borders'; Jerusalem and statehood clauses appear in the treaties with the PLO (15 Feb 2000) and the State of Palestine (26 Jun 2015).

The Holy See's opposition was spent and complained of (League notes 1922; resolution 303 in 1949; 45 years without recognition; Shamir 1987: Israel 'can do nothing but express its unhappiness'), but rarely changed outcomes.
Theology and diplomacy separated: Nostra Aetate (1965) rejected the deicide charge; the 1985 Notes placed the State of Israel under 'the common principles of international law'.

Status as of October 2026: Holy See–Israel relations intact; new nuncio Lingua appointed 22 Jan 2026; economic agreement unsigned (last communiqué 14 Jun 2017); Parolin at UNGA Sept 2026 restated two states and an internationally guaranteed Jerusalem.

entries.topic: Open questions as of October 2026 and dates to watch

claims.text: Leo XIV's 2026 travel page lists journeys to Monaco (28 Mar), Africa (13–23 Apr), Spain (6–12 Jun), France and UNESCO (25–28 Sep) and Uruguay, Argentina and Peru (6–17 Nov 2026); no visit to Israel or Palestine is listed as of October 2026.

Open as of October 2026: Becciu renewed proceedings, hearing 29 Oct 2026 (defendants presumed innocent); ICI 2006–2011 recovery payments due 30 Oct 2026, no figures published; Orlandi parliamentary commission (Law 202/2023) has not reported; Rome prosecutors' inquiry open.

The Pius XII files (to Oct 1958) opened 2 Mar 2020; Rioli's 2024 chapter on the Pius XII papers and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict is the first study on the subject; no opening date announced for John XXIII's papers; the 1947 Sneh–Tardini account cites no archive.
